source_text: βολον ἐναργὲς ἦν, ὡς ἔν γε τῷ ἁγίῳ βαπτίσματι καὶ ἡμεῖς αὐτοὶ πληροῦν εὐχόμεθα διὰ πίστεως. Ὡς γὰρ αὐτός που πάλιν ὁ θεσπέσιος ἔφη Παῦλος, «Συνετάφημεν γὰρ αὐτῷ διὰ τοῦ βαπτίσματος εἰς τὸν θάνατον, ἵνα ὥσπερ ἠγέρθη Χριστὸς διὰ τῆς δόξης τοῦ
pass_b_english: Cyril: …clear symbol it was, as at least in the holy baptism we ourselves also pray to fulfill through faith. For as somewhere again all-divine Paul himself said, ‘For we have been buried-together with him through the baptism unto the death, that just as Christ was raised through the glory of the Father, so also we may walk in newness of life.’ (Romans 6:4) And he said again: ‘Always carrying around the putting-to-death of Jesus in the body, that also the life of Jesus may be manifested in our mortal flesh.’ (2 Corinthians 4:10)
Palladius: And what then is the putting-to-death of Christ said here?

Cyril: The having died to world and sins, and to live through a sacred and holy and as-much-as-possible God-beloved life, upon which again Paul was being very solemnized saying: ‘For I through law died to law, that I may live to God; I have been co-crucified with Christ. And I no longer live, and Christ lives in me. And what I now live in flesh, I live in faith of the Son of God who has loved me, and handed himself over for me.’ (Galatians 2:19–20) This, I think, is… according to law. So then the removal of hairs hints the cleansing of mind, which the divine and sharper word of God would work in us. And washing-off of garments shows for us a bright and unadulterated citizenship, the outwardly-appearing. ‘For taking-thought good things, not only before Lord,’ (Hebrews 4:12) according to what has been written, ‘but also before humans.’ (Romans 12:17) And he himself somewhere says: ‘Let your light shine before the humans, that they may see your good (Matthew 5:16) (Galatians 2:20)
